To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the contractile function during reperfusion was not improved by adenosine, but deteriorated by AICAR.
the postischemia infusion of adenosine or AICAR did not improve the systolic function of reperfusing myocardium, although the ATP tissue content was increased by these agents.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of adenosine on the contractility of the heart.

the question whether the postischaemic repletion of adenosine-triphosphate (ATP)-deficit by precursor infusion is beneficial in terms of regional systolic contractile function of the reperfused myocardial tissue.

the question of whether a repletion of adenosine-triphosphate (ATP), the energy source of myocardium, can be achieved by means of precursor infusions and whether this repletion has any beneficial effect on the contractile function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the postischemia infusion of adenosine or AICAR has no beneficial effects on the postischemically depressed regional contractile function.
the ATP level of reperfused tissue does not correlate to contractile function, and that the ATP content of the reperfused tissue is not an appropriate marker of the metabolic state of the tissue.
the reperfusion dysfunction is not due to a lack of energy supply but to a failure of energy utilization.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the reperfusion of ischemically preconditioned tissue with an increased ATP content does not result in improved regional systolic function.
the postischemically increased ATP production by adenosine is not beneficial for the contractility of reperfused ischemic myocardium.
a reperfusion dysfunction is not necessarily associated with a low energy level.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ATP content is a poor marker for contractile function in the reperfused myocardium.
the postischemia infusion of adenosine or AICAR is not beneficial for the recovery of contractile function in the reperfused myocardial tissue.
the repletion of ATP by adenosine is not beneficial for the contractility of reperfused ischemic myocardium.
